name: MT9196
full_name: MT9196 Integrated Digital Phone Circuit (IDPC) -- programmable u-Law/A-Law codec + filters
subcategory: telephony codec / integrated digital phone circuit
description: Zarlink (formerly Mitel) ISO2-CMOS Integrated Digital Phone Circuit for digital telephone sets, wireless phones, and local-area comms stations. A single-5V mixed-signal SoC combining a programmable u-Law/A-Law (CCITT G.711) filter/codec, digital gain pads, DTMF and single-tone generation, a tone ringer, and fully-differential handset + speakerphone transducer interfaces (mic amps, handset speaker driver, speakerphone driver, anti-howl for group listening). The digital side speaks ST-BUS/SSI (GCI-compatible) with internal registers accessed over a serial microport compatible with Intel or Motorola/National host conventions.

PDIP-28 / SOIC-28.notes: PDIP-28 (MT9196AE) and SOIC-28 (MT9196AS) share this pin numbering. A PLCC-28 variant (MT9196AP) exists with different, package-specific numbering -- see the datasheet Figure 2.

extra.device_class: integrated digital phone circuit (IDPC), mixed-signal telephony SoC
extra.codec: programmable u-Law / A-Law, CCITT G.711 and sign-magnitude coding
extra.features: digital gain pads (+21/-24 dB Tx & Rx, 3.0 dB steps), DTMF + single-tone generation, tone ringer, anti-howl for group listening
extra.transducers: fully-differential handset mic + speaker, speakerphone speaker, on-hook answer-back mic, auxiliary analog port
extra.digital_interface: ST-BUS / SSI (GCI-compatible); serial microport (Intel or Motorola/National host modes)
extra.master_clock: 4.096 MHz crystal (XSTL2 + CLOCKin) or 4 MHz master clock in SSI-async

typical_application: Digital telephone sets, wireless (cordless) telephones, and local-area communication stations: converts received PCM to analog audio and mic audio to PCM, with on-chip gain, DTMF/tone generation, and handset/speakerphone drive, all under host control over the serial microport.
gotchas: Pin 6 (IC, 'internal connection') MUST be tied to VSS for normal operation -- leaving it floating misbehaves.

The serial microport has two host conventions: in Intel mode DATA1 carries both transmit and receive and DATA2 is disconnected; in Motorola/National mode DATA1 is transmit-only and DATA2 is receive. Wiring for the wrong convention breaks register access.
IRQ (pin 13) is an open-drain, active-low output -- it needs an external pull-up.
Single +5 V part; the digital pins are TTL/CMOS level. VRef and VBias are internal analog references (VDD/2 area) -- decouple each with 0.1 uF to VSSA, do not load them.
Master clock is a 4.096 MHz crystal (not 4 MHz) on XSTL2/CLOCKin in the crystal configuration; 4 MHz applies only to the SSI-asynchronous external-clock mode.
Zarlink/Mitel is defunct (line went Mitel -> Zarlink -> Microsemi -> Microchip); this is legacy telecom silicon, sourced NOS/surplus.
